issues.title: [HARDWARE] Dynamic Thermal Throttling & Load Shedding
issues.body:
### Context

The Floating Tank is a sealed enclosure in a Michigan wetland, and in summer the inside of it can pass what the Jetson is rated for. Nothing on the station reacts to that: it runs the same workload however hot it gets. Thermal management means watching the `jtop` thermal stats and, when a threshold is crossed, shedding load in order — video processing first, since it is the heaviest, then down to audio only — and recording that it happened, without waiting for a human to notice.

The planes this rides on already exist. Every unit runs with systemd `MemoryAccounting` and a soft `MemoryHigh` cap, so the memory half of load-shedding has a seam; agent health flows over the EventBus ABC and the `orpheus_health` KV plane, and presence uses KV-TTL. Thermal events belong on those, not on a channel of their own.

### ASRs

- A thermal manager reads CPU and GPU temperature and reports which shedding level the station is at: normal, video shed, non-essential shed, emergency shutdown.
- Thresholds are additive config — `thermal.shed_video_at_c`, `thermal.shed_nonessential_at_c`, `thermal.emergency_shutdown_at_c` — and default off, per the Reversibility Contract.
- Shedding acts through systemd, the same mechanism an operator uses, so recovering by hand is never fighting the manager.
- Hysteresis: a shed service comes back only once the temperature is 5°C below the threshold that shed it.
- `jtop` missing is logged and otherwise ignored. Never guess a temperature.
- Thermal status and shedding actions publish on the health plane and appear in Diagnostics.

### Definition of Done

A simulated thermal ramp sheds and restores services in order with hysteresis, the events are visible on the health plane and in Diagnostics, and every knob is additive and default-off.

issues.title: [INFRA] Contributor Guardrail Automation
issues.body:
### Context

An open-source repository leans on settings nothing in the tree can see: branch protection on `main`, required reviews, and the community health files. They are easy to misconfigure, and today nothing would notice if one drifted.

This is the GitHub repo-settings half only. The mechanical guardrails inside the tree already exist and are not this issue — `scripts/check_guardrails.py`, `make guardrails`, and an always-on CI job enforce agent wiring, manifest catalog coverage, docs-site nav, and non-negotiable-count coherence. Some of what is left needs the admin API, so parts of it are owner-gated.

### ASRs

- `scripts/verify-repo-guardrails.sh` uses `gh` to check branch protection, review requirements, and the presence of the community health files.
- It exits 0 when everything passes and 1 when anything does not, so CI can gate on it, and prints a report a human can read.
- A weekly workflow runs it and raises an alert when a setting has drifted.
- `make verify-guardrails` wraps it, like every other entry point here.

### Definition of Done

A fresh clone plus `make verify-guardrails` reports the repository's guardrail state truthfully, the weekly job files an alert on drift, and CONTRIBUTING says how to run it.

issues.title: [INFRA] PyPI Publishing Pipeline (Common + Agents)
issues.body:
### Context

Orpheus components are only consumable by cloning the repository. Publishing `orpheus-common` and each agent as independent packages opens the door to third-party integrations, reuse in other wildlife-monitoring projects, and a dependency model for someone who wants one piece rather than the whole station. The goal is that `pip install orpheus-agent-bird-detection` works.

The groundwork is in place. Every Python component already carries a PEP 517 `pyproject.toml` with a setuptools backend, a dynamic version read from its `VERSION` file, and a name following the `orpheus-<component-type>-<name>` convention; agents already declare `orpheus-common>=0.2.0` as a dependency, which only resolves once it is on an index. What is missing is everything between a valid `pyproject.toml` and a package a stranger can install.

### ASRs

- Hardware-specific dependencies (ALSA, PortAudio, GPIO, CUDA) move into optional extras such as `[jetson]`, so a package installs cleanly on a developer machine that has none of them.
- Every component's wheel builds in CI, and a failed build fails the pull request.
- TestPyPI takes the pre-release publish, so the install path is exercised before PyPI sees it.
- Each component's README works as a PyPI long description — no repo-relative image paths.
- The declared `requires-python` stays honest: the packages claim exactly the interpreters they are tested against, and nothing here quietly raises the Jetson's floor.
- Packages install standalone. No monorepo install tool, no editable-path assumptions.

### Acceptance Criteria

```gherkin
Feature: PyPI Publishing Pipeline

  Scenario: Install orpheus-common from PyPI
    Given orpheus-common has been published to PyPI
    When running "pip install orpheus-common" in a clean environment
    Then the package installs without errors on every interpreter its metadata declares
    And pip refuses cleanly on the ones it does not

  Scenario: Install agent from PyPI
    Given orpheus-agent-bird-detection has been published to PyPI
    When running "pip install orpheus-agent-bird-detection"
    Then the package installs with orpheus-common as a transitive dependency

  Scenario: Hardware extras install cleanly on a developer machine
    Given a machine with no ALSA, PortAudio, or GPIO libraries
    When running "pip install orpheus-agent-audio-motion"
    Then the package installs without them
    And the [jetson] extra can be installed separately on Jetson hardware

  Scenario: Build wheel in CI
    Given a PR modifies any file in platform/orpheus-common
    When the CI pipeline runs
    Then "python -m build --wheel" succeeds for orpheus-common
    And the wheel is uploaded to TestPyPI as a pre-release artifact
```

### Definition of Done

- [ ] Hardware-specific dependencies moved into `[jetson]` extras across the agents that have them.
- [ ] A CI step validates `python -m build --wheel` for every component on each pull request.
- [ ] TestPyPI publication configured for pre-release validation.
- [ ] Component READMEs render correctly as PyPI long descriptions.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` documents how to release a new package version.

issues.title: [INFRA] Release workflow: publish a tagged component to PyPI
issues.body:
### Context

Cutting a release is manual. `.github/workflows/release.yml` exists, but a `v*.*.*` tag only produces a GitHub Release with a generated changelog — nothing builds or publishes a package.

Change detection is already solved on the test side: `pr-tests.yml` runs `dorny/paths-filter` and gates each component's job on it, so a pull request touching one agent runs that agent's suite and a change to `orpheus-common` runs everything downstream. The publish half is what is missing.

### ASRs

- A component-scoped tag (`orpheus-agent-bird-detection/v0.5.0`) builds and publishes exactly that component; an `orpheus-common` release also rebuilds the agents that depend on it, in dependency order.
- Publishing uses OIDC trusted publishing. No long-lived PyPI token lives in repository secrets.
- Release jobs are idempotent: re-running a failed one must not double-publish.
- The existing repository-wide `v*.*.*` behaviour survives unchanged.

### Acceptance Criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Release a component from a tag

  Scenario: A component tag publishes only that component
    Given a tag "orpheus-agent-bird-detection/v0.5.0" is pushed
    When the release workflow runs
    Then only orpheus-agent-bird-detection is built and published to PyPI
    And other components are not touched

  Scenario: OIDC trusted publishing is used for the upload
    Given the release workflow is triggered by a component tag
    When the PyPI upload step runs
    Then no API token secret is used — OIDC authentication is used
    And the upload is auditable via PyPI's trusted publisher log

  Scenario: Re-running a failed release does not double-publish
    Given a release job failed after uploading one component
    When the job is re-run
    Then the version already on PyPI is not uploaded again
    And the run completes without error
```

### Definition of Done

- [ ] `.github/workflows/release.yml` extended: a component tag builds that component's wheel and publishes it.
- [ ] OIDC trusted publishing configured in the PyPI project settings for each package.
- [ ] Downstream ordering handled — an `orpheus-common` release rebuilds its dependents.
- [ ] `docs/RELEASING.md` documents the end-to-end release and how to cut a hotfix.

issues.title: [CORE] Event-sourcing: the DB as a projection of the durable consciousness stream
issues.body:
### Context
Status 2026-08: the durable log's FIRST WRITER shipped — flag-gated `event_sourcing.shadow_publish_enabled` (default off) publishes detections to a bounded JetStream stream alongside the SQLite save. This item is the read half: projection + replay.
With durable JetStream streams the event log becomes the source of truth and the DB a projection (the existing `replay.py` is the seed).

### Scope
A JetStream-stream loader for `ReplayEngine` (load from a stream, reuse `_ReplayEvent`/`play`); rebuild DB state by replaying the log; build a NEW derived view by replaying history; bootstrap a fresh actor from the past. Steal Akka Persistence's journal+snapshot split so replay doesn't start from genesis.

### Definition of Done
Replay a stream → state rebuilt; a new projection built purely by replay; verified in the Simulacrum. Refs ADR 0017.

issues.title: [REFACTOR] Remove the MQTT backend after the NATS Jetson soak
issues.body:
### Context
ADR 0017: MQTT is a removable fallback, not a co-equal backend — its features have no JetStream-parity value, so maintaining two real backends is sunk cost. **Gate status 2026-08-22: the NATS Jetson soak is DONE** — flywheel_1 cutover ran NATS as the production transport (mosquitto retired from the box; `install-backbone` removes the legacy `orpheus-mqtt` unit). Removal is now unblocked, sequenced AFTER the public-Orpheus merge so the merge itself stays a validated snapshot.

### Scope
Delete the mqtt backend (`_make_mqtt_bus`, the `MQTTClient` EventBus path) + the `paho-mqtt` dependency + the mosquitto fallback install; collapse to the nats backend. KEEP the EventBus ABC (it's the injection seam, not sunk cost).

### Definition of Done
nats-only; paho removed; tests updated; reversible by revert. Refs ADR 0017.

issues.title: [DEVOPS] Simulacrum: slim images, x86 validation, and a timed cold start
issues.body:
### Context

Most of the original scope shipped and is live-verified: the UI and classifier agents run behind the `fleet` compose profile with models mounted, `SIM_MODE=replay` replays `artifacts/audio-samples/` as audio.motion so real BirdNET/PANNs output reaches the correlator inside containers — the deterministic sign-off the laptop verification runbook uses — and each service has a healthcheck. This is the tail.

Hot-reload inside the containers is out of scope: the host `make dev-stack` owns the live-reload loop.

### Scope

- Multi-stage slim Dockerfiles. The fleet images are heavy first-builds today.
- Verify the x86_64 path. arm64 is proven; this wants CI or a documented x86 run.
- A clone-to-running time that has actually been measured rather than asserted.

### Definition of Done

Slim images; x86 validated; a fresh-clone `make sim-up` timed on a real laptop with the measured number written into the Operator's Manual. Under five minutes is the target; if it cannot be met, the documented number is the honest one.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Read-only mirror host: serving stack + public portal
issues.body:
### Context
Heavy dashboard reads contend with agent writes on the live SQLite, and public sharing must never expose the production box. The push-only replication path already exists in code: snapshot (`VACUUM INTO`) + rate-limit/query-timeout hardening shipped, and the UI backend honors `ui.read_from_replica` + `mirror.staging_path` (read-only DetectionDB). What remains is the serving stack on the mirror host — and it unblocks the Epic 2 read-only MCP server.

### Scope
- `docker-compose.mirror.yml` (or systemd equivalent): read-only FastAPI/UI over the replica, replica refresh unit/timer, no broker required (agents' remote-broker `connect_required` heuristic already tolerates absence).
- Public HTML frontend for the data-only export, flag-gated behind `public.enabled` (default off).
- LLM context-dump command (the portal's machine-readable export).

### ASRs
- The replica is the ONLY data source on the mirror host; read-only enforced at the DB layer (`read_only=True` skips schema init — already the code's contract).
- Zero writes ever flow mirror->Jetson.
- Additive config only; everything default-off per the Reversibility Contract.

### Definition of Done
A second host serves the dashboard + portal from the replica while the Jetson runs untouched; the MCP item's blocker is lifted; runbook for standing one up.

### Current state: stubbed

The snapshot CLI works and the UI honours a read-only replica, but no `orpheus-mirror` systemd unit ships and no make target installs or starts one. `mirror.enabled` therefore gates nothing continuous: setting it true and rebooting produces no snapshots, and the UI falls back to the live database with a warning, so the failure is quiet.

This shipped as scaffolding, not as a finished feature — it was not merged as done because it had not been thought through far enough. Anyone picking it up is welcome to do it better than the sketch suggests, including changing the seam if the seam is wrong. The bar for merging the finished version is the same as for anything else here.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Citizen-science export bundles (Slice 1: local bundle builder)
issues.body:
### Context
Twice-asked owner priority: turn detections into upload-ready contribution packages a HUMAN submits. Platform reality (rule #7 — look it up, don't guess): eBird/Macaulay and Xeno-canto are web-upload-only; iNaturalist has an API but forbids bot/bulk posting. So the deliverable is a local bundle builder — never an auto-poster.

### Scope
`orpheus_common/contributions/`: bundle builder (clip + metadata) + per-platform sidecar formatters + an `orpheus-export` CLI. Off-by-default, zero network/auth, local files only. License/threshold/OAuth policy decisions stay owner-gated for later slices.

### Definition of Done
`orpheus-export <detection|entity id>` produces a bundle with the audio clip + a per-platform sidecar; round-trip tests; documented in the User Guide.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Year-range history aggregates: summary tables or mirror offload (escalation path)
issues.body:
### Context
The 2026-08 perf batch fixed the measured pain (31.6s bird-correlation page): history/stats endpoints now aggregate from raw rows (no per-row model materialisation) over covering indexes, and SQL was measured sub-second at 30-day windows on the production DB. This item is the ESCALATION PATH, to be built only if year-range windows still lag on real hardware.

### Scope (evidence-gated — measure first)
- (a) Summary tables refreshed by the existing maintenance/cleanup tick — NEVER triggers (nothing may tax the agents' write transactions).
- (b) Or move heavy analytics to the read-only mirror host entirely.
- Owner constraint: no copy-pasted SQL — shared query shapes live once (helpers or plain SQLite VIEWs; views are free saved queries, not materialised).

### Definition of Done
Year-range timings measured on the Jetson first; if built, outputs byte-identical to the live aggregation; write path untouched.

issues.title: [INFRA] Deploy-path hardening: clean-copy UI install, gps in the service loops, --no-index local installs
issues.body:
### Context

Four defects in the install path, found while deploying this branch to a real station. Three remain.

1. **The UI installer builds from the git checkout.** `npm install` runs inside the working tree, so a deploy leaves `services/orpheus_ui/frontend/package-lock.json` modified. The installer should build from a clean copy, or use `npm ci` against a copy, so deploying never dirties the tree it deployed from.

2. **First-party installs can reach the network.** The deploy installs local packages by path; adding `--no-index` to those pip invocations makes it structurally impossible for the resolver to fetch a same-named package from an index. Today it fails loudly instead, because `orpheus-common` is not published — a property worth having rather than a coincidence worth relying on. Note this interacts with dependency resolution: the platform install must still be able to fetch orpheus-common's third-party dependencies, so `--no-index` belongs on the first-party path only.

3. **The frontend deploy copies over the deployed static directory additively.** A file removed from the Vite build is not removed from the deployed tree, so stale assets accumulate. Confirmed on the station: `vite.svg` is gone from the source and `index.html` now references `/orpheus-mark.svg`, but the deployed `static/vite.svg` is still there and still serves 200 with nothing linking to it. The frontend step should `rsync --delete` into the static directory, or clear it before copying.

### Definition of Done

A deploy leaves the source tree clean, and the first-party installs cannot resolve against a package index while third-party dependencies still install normally.

issues.title: [HARDWARE] Retention steady-state review: size-trigger economics on the data disk
issues.body:
### Context
Verified in code + on the box (2026-08-22): the age knobs (`raw_audio_days`, etc.) have NO production callers — only the size trigger runs (95% of `max_size_gb`=700, per directory). Post-cutover, audio-motion moved from its agent-local 50GB cap to the shared 700GB knob, so audio cleanup stalls for ~97 days (~620GB growth at ~6.4GB/day). Snapshots hold a 547-day window (~750GB steady state); timelapses have NO cleanup code at all (their `retention_days` is log-only). Combined steady state exceeds the 1.8T data disk within roughly a year.

### Scope
After the default-behavior soak: decide deliberate per-directory caps (or implement age-based enforcement and a timelapser cleanup), sized so the projected steady state fits the disk with margin. Cleanup ticks already log their effective policy — keep the decision observable.

### Definition of Done
Projected steady state fits the disk with documented margin; policy in the Operator's Manual; no surprise deletions (changes announced by the policy log line before they act).

Related: *[FEATURE] Enforce the file-retention age window* is the mechanism; this story decides the numbers.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Dashboard: per-service CPU/memory panel
issues.body:
### Context
Operators want per-process resource visibility in the GUI. The accounting already exists: every unit runs with systemd `MemoryAccounting=yes` (and `MemoryHigh` caps on the model agents), so the numbers are free to read.

### Scope
- Backend endpoint reading `systemctl show -p MemoryCurrent,CPUUsageNSec` (or /sys/fs/cgroup) for the orpheus units; served alongside the existing Service Status card.
- Frontend panel next to Service Status; polls at the HEALTH tier.
- macOS dev fallback: psutil against the dev-stack pidfiles, or hide the panel entirely (the weather-card precedent).

### Definition of Done
Panel shows live RSS + CPU per unit on the Jetson; hides gracefully where unsupported; zero new dependencies for the agents themselves.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Mobile-first UX polish for the dashboard
issues.body:
### Context

The dashboard is the product on phones too — a native app would just wrap this page, so the investment goes into making the web UI excellent on mobile instead (owner direction; supersedes the closed mobile-app concept).

### ASRs

- Audit every page at phone widths: navigation, tables (horizontal scroll containers, not page scroll), charts, filters, tap targets.
- Fix the top offenders; add a viewport/PWA manifest so add-to-home-screen behaves like an app.
- E2E mobile viewport tests exist (playwright mobile project) — extend them to pin the fixes.

### Definition of Done

All pages usable one-handed on a phone; mobile playwright suite green; no horizontal page scroll anywhere.

issues.title: [SPIKE] Isolate Individual Bird Calls from Overlapped Audio
issues.body:
### Context

When several birds vocalise at once, a clip yields one blended classification and the correlator sees a single detection where there were two animals. The tractable half of this problem shipped: intra-clip temporal localisation (ADR 0011) records WHEN each call occurs inside a clip via `TemporalInterval` / `intervals_json`, and the correlator clusters on those bounds. What has never been built is separation of calls that OVERLAP in time.

### The question this spike answers

Is time-frequency source separation worth it on the Jetson for overlapping vocalisations, or is temporal localisation plus per-interval classification good enough?

### ASRs

- Assemble a small labelled set of genuinely overlapped clips from `artifacts/audio-samples` plus real captures.
- Measure the current pipeline's failure rate on them (blended label, dropped second bird).
- Evaluate at least one separation approach against Jetson constraints: unified LPDDR5 shared with the detection GPU, ARM64 wheels, inference budget alongside BirdNET/PANNs/AVES.

### Definition of Done

A written decision (ADR or design doc) with the measured baseline, the evaluated option(s), and a build-or-drop recommendation. No production code required.

issues.title: [HARDWARE] Implement MCP Server for ALSA Audio Playback
issues.body:
### Context

The playback agent (`orpheus-agent-audio-playback`) plays audio on request over the event bus. What does not exist is an MCP server exposing that capability as tools an LLM can call.

Architecture note: MCP servers run OFF the Jetson, on the mirror/portal host, so they are not bound by the Jetson's Python floor and cannot contend for its GPU/RAM. The playback capability is reached over the NATS backplane (request-reply is already on the EventBus ABC), not by importing agent code.

### ASRs

- MCP server exposing playback as tools (list available sounds, play a sound on a channel, stop).
- Calls travel over the backplane's request-reply surface; the server holds no ALSA handle itself.
- Safety: rate limits and an explicit allow-list of playable assets; no arbitrary file paths.

### Definition of Done

An MCP client can enumerate and trigger playback through the server against a running station; unsafe requests are refused; the server runs on the portal host with no Jetson-side changes beyond configuration.

issues.title: [SAFETY] Hardware Circuit Breakers via MCP Middleware
issues.body:
### Context

Once actuation is reachable by an LLM (playback today, more later), the system needs limits that hold regardless of what the caller asks for: no runaway playback loops, no output during quiet hours, no unbounded actuation rate.

This is middleware in front of the MCP tool surface, not per-tool checks — a tool added later must inherit the limits by construction.

### ASRs

- Declarative policy (rate, quiet hours, per-tool ceilings) read from config with safe defaults.
- Breaker state is observable: an operator can see when a breaker tripped and why.
- Tripping is fail-safe (deny), and denials are logged actionably.

### Definition of Done

Actuation tools are only reachable through the middleware; a synthetic runaway caller is stopped by the breaker and the trip is visible in diagnostics.
depends_on: [HARDWARE] Implement MCP Server for ALSA Audio Playback

issues.title: [FEATURE] Agentic Audio Auto-Tuning via MCP
issues.body:
### Context

Audio-motion thresholds (`threshold_db`, `margin_db`, holdoff) are hand-tuned per site and drift with season and weather. The station already publishes what a tuner would need: per-channel levels, XRUN counts, trigger rates, and the detection cascade's yield.

Depends on the MCP server and the safety middleware — auto-tuning is actuation on configuration.

### ASRs

- Read side: expose channel telemetry and detection yield as MCP resources.
- Write side: propose config changes through the config service (versioned, auditable, revertible), never by editing YAML in place.
- Every change is attributable and bounded by the safety middleware.

### Definition of Done

An agent can observe a mis-tuned channel, propose a bounded threshold change, and have it applied through the versioned config path with a visible audit trail and a one-command revert.
depends_on: [HARDWARE] Implement MCP Server for ALSA Audio Playback

issues.title: [FEATURE] Human Wake-Word Integration
issues.body:
### Context

The station listens continuously but has no way for a person standing in front of it to address it. A wake word turns the microphones into an interface without adding a screen.

### ASRs

- On-device wake-word detection in the audio path, cheap enough to run alongside the classifiers on the Jetson.
- A detection publishes an event on the backplane like any other detection; downstream behaviour is a separate concern.
- Off by default and clearly documented — always-on human speech capture is a privacy decision, not a default.

### Definition of Done

Speaking the wake word near a station publishes a wake event with acceptable false-positive rate over a soak; the feature is off unless explicitly enabled. Pairs with human-audio privacy filtering.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Privacy & Human Anomaly Filtering
issues.body:
### Context

Outdoor microphones capture human conversation. Today human-labelled sounds are suppressed from BIRD results (`is_bird_sound` / non-bird label filtering), but the underlying audio clip is still written to disk and retained like any other capture. Suppressing a label is not privacy.

This matters more as clips move off-box: the read-only mirror and citizen-science export both ship real audio.

### ASRs

- Detect human speech in a capture and act on the CLIP, not just the label: skip persisting, or persist a redacted/degraded version, per policy.
- Policy is config-driven with a privacy-preserving default once enabled, and the choice is documented for operators.
- Anything exported or mirrored inherits the filter — no path that bypasses it.

### Definition of Done

With filtering enabled, a clip containing human speech does not reach disk in intelligible form, wildlife detections in the same window are unaffected, and the mirror/export paths are covered by tests.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Weatherproof Field Display for the Floating Tank
issues.body:
### Context

At the installation itself there is no way to see what the station is hearing — the dashboard lives on a laptop or phone elsewhere. A weatherproof display at the site shows current detections to whoever is standing there.

### ASRs

- Outdoor-rated display and enclosure; power and cabling specified alongside the existing station hardware.
- Renders a kiosk view of the existing UI (no second frontend): sunlight-readable, no interaction required, degrades to a last-known-good view if the backend is unreachable.
- Survives the same conditions the station does; documented in the hardware guide.

### Definition of Done

A display at the installation shows live detections continuously through a full weather cycle, driven by the existing UI with no separate rendering stack.

issues.title: [REFACTOR] OpenTelemetry: instrument the cascade end to end
issues.body:
### Context

Partially shipped. `orpheus_common.telemetry` exists with optional `opentelemetry-sdk` / OTLP exporter dependencies and its own tests, so a station CAN emit OTel signals. What is missing is the migration itself: the components still carry their own metrics/logging conventions, and there is no end-to-end trace across the detection cascade.

### Remaining scope (reduced to what is actually left)

- Instrument the cascade so one audio.motion event yields a single trace spanning classifier agents and the correlator, carried over the backplane.
- Converge component metrics on the telemetry module rather than per-agent ad hoc counters.
- Keep the optional dependency optional: absent OTel packages must remain a no-op, not an import error.
- Document the collector/exporter setup for an operator who wants it, off by default.

### Definition of Done

A detection cascade produces one connected trace in a collector; components emit through the shared telemetry surface; stations without the OTel extras behave exactly as before.

### Current state: stubbed

`orpheus_common.telemetry` is complete and tested — a no-op tracer fallback, a real OTLP/HTTP exporter, optional dependencies — and nothing calls it. There are zero `setup_tracing()` calls and zero span sites in the tree, so enabling `telemetry.enabled` emits nothing at all.

The exporter plumbing being done is why this is worth finishing rather than restarting. Calling setup once per process is trivial. The work that needs thought is what to instrument and, above all, **propagating trace context across the bus in message headers** so one detection chain (audio.motion → classify → correlate → entity) is a single trace instead of four unrelated ones — plus binding trace and span ids into structlog so logs and traces line up.

Until spans actually emit, nothing in this repo should claim OpenTelemetry traces as a feature.

This shipped as scaffolding, not as a finished feature — it was not merged as done because it had not been thought through far enough. Anyone picking it up is welcome to do it better than the sketch suggests, including changing the seam if the seam is wrong. The bar for merging the finished version is the same as for anything else here.

issues.title: [SPIKE] Modern Python on the Jetson — can we drop the 3.9 floor?
issues.body:
### Context

The platform pins `requires-python = ">=3.9, <3.10"` because the ARM64 ML wheels that work on the Jetson's vendor image required it. Everything downstream inherits that floor: dependency versions age, some upstream security fixes ship only for newer Python, and contributors on modern machines run an interpreter nobody else uses.

The foundation is now solid enough to test the assumption instead of inheriting it.

### Definition of Done

- Timeboxed. On the real Jetson, establish whether a current CPython runs the stack: install a modern interpreter alongside the pinned one, build/resolve each component's dependencies, and run the model agents against real audio.
- Record what breaks, per dependency: no ARM64 wheel, CUDA/JetPack binding, or source build that fails.
- Verdict written down either way — 'we can move, here is the migration' or 'we cannot, here is exactly what blocks it and what would unblock it'.
- If it works, a follow-up issue with the migration plan; if not, this becomes the citable answer next time it is asked.

### Notes

Spike, not a migration. Do not change the floor in this issue.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Contribute recordings upstream to the models we use
issues.body:
### Context

Orpheus runs public models trained on public datasets. A station accumulates exactly the material those datasets want — labelled, localised, real-world recordings — and there is currently no path for an operator to give any of it back.

Distinct from the citizen-science export (observations to observation platforms). This is about improving the models themselves, where the licence and terms of the upstream corpus permit contribution.

### Definition of Done

- Survey the upstream corpora behind the shipped models and record, per corpus, whether contribution is permitted and by what mechanism.
- For those that permit it: a per-clip flow the operator drives — select, review, confirm, submit.
- Explicit consent per submission. No bulk, no background upload, no default-on. A clip may contain a neighbour's conversation; the operator decides, every time.
- Strip or bucket site metadata by the same fail-closed rules as the public projection.
- Documented in the User Guide, including what leaves the box.

### Notes

Rule #7 applies to platform terms: read them, do not infer them.

issues.title: [DOCS] Keep the project comparison page accurate
issues.body:
### Context

`docs/comparison.md` states plainly where Orpheus fits against the other projects in this space, including where they are the better choice. Those projects keep improving, so the page decays unless someone checks it.

A good first contribution: it needs judgement and honesty rather than deep familiarity with the codebase.

### Definition of Done

- Each claim about another project verified against its current documentation.
- Anything stale corrected; anything unfair rewritten or removed.
- New alternatives worth naming are added, with the same even hand.

### Notes

Accuracy beats flattery. If a competitor is simply better for a reader, the page should say so.

issues.title: [SAFETY] A human gate on every auto-discovery equivalence promotion
issues.body:
### Context

The correlator's auto-discovery worker runs by default and can learn a false equivalence between two taxonomy identifiers, then promote it to `accepted` and act on it live. A wrong merge silently folds two species into one entity stream. The most dangerous slice — same-namespace merges — is already guardable with `correlation.auto_discovery.cross_namespace_accept_only`, but there is no way to require a human on every promotion.

The visibility half is built. The `orpheus/system/auto-discovery/health` subject has a UI subscriber behind `/api/auto-discovery/status`, and `diagnose_equivalences()` is served at `/api/equivalences/diagnose`. What is left is the gate itself.

### ASRs

- `correlation.auto_discovery.auto_accept: false` sends every candidate to `pending_review` for the Equivalences queue instead of accepting it, whatever the namespaces.
- The default preserves today's behaviour, like the cross-namespace guard beside it — an operator opts into the stricter setting.
- The worker logs which policy it applied, so a gated run is distinguishable from an ungated one without reading the journal.

### Definition of Done

- `correlation.auto_discovery` gains a mode that queues every promotion for review instead of accepting any automatically, and it is the documented setting for an unattended station.
- With that mode on, a discovered pair never reaches `accepted` without an explicit operator action, and the pending queue shows what is waiting.
- The existing cross-namespace guard keeps working unchanged for operators who do not turn the gate on.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Enforce detections_days — retention for database rows
issues.body:
### Context

`storage.retention.detections_days` is read and validated at startup and then ignored: retention only ever deletes clip files, never detection rows. On a station running for a year the database grows without bound while the config claims a 365-day window. The setting should either work or stop pretending to exist.

### ASRs

- A cleanup pass deletes detection rows older than the configured window, in bounded batches, without blocking the writers.
- Entities and their evidence links stay consistent — no orphaned references.
- The pass logs the effective policy and the row count it removed, in the same shape as the clip cleanup.
- Disabled by default until an operator sets a window.

### Definition of Done

Database growth respects the configured retention, and the disk-headroom story covers rows as well as files.

### Current state: stubbed

`storage.retention.detections_days` is parsed and validated at startup and then read by nothing. Only clip files are ever cleaned up, so the database grows without bound while the configuration claims a window.

This shipped as scaffolding, not as a finished feature — it was not merged as done because it had not been thought through far enough. Anyone picking it up is welcome to do it better than the sketch suggests, including changing the seam if the seam is wrong. The bar for merging the finished version is the same as for anything else here.

issues.title: [REFACTOR] Move the remaining hand-rolled agents onto the Actor base
issues.body:
### Context

The `Actor` base owns bus connection, heartbeats, signal handling, shutdown, and stats. The detection agents use it; `video-snapshotter` and `video-timelapser` do not, and `audio-motion`, `audio-playback`, and `video-motion` still hand-roll parts of the lifecycle around it. Each hand-rolled copy is a place for the health and shutdown behaviour to drift.

### ASRs

- Every long-running agent constructs an `Actor` and inherits lifecycle, heartbeat, and stats from it.
- Per-agent code keeps only what is genuinely specific to that agent.
- Existing e2e bus oracles stay green — observable behaviour on the bus does not change.

### Definition of Done

- `video-snapshotter` and `video-timelapser` construct an `Actor`; `audio-motion`, `audio-playback`, and `video-motion` no longer hand-roll connection, heartbeat, signal handling, shutdown, or stats.
- Each converted agent's existing tests pass unchanged, and its health payload keeps the same shape.
- Grepping for a second heartbeat or shutdown implementation across the agents returns nothing.

issues.title: [CORE] Act on the latent memory — an active-inference consumer
issues.body:
### Context

The state-space memory records when each entity tends to appear and can answer `query_likelihood`, but nothing reads it. The write half shipped without the payoff half: the system remembers, and then does nothing with the memory.

### ASRs

- A consumer uses temporal likelihood to pre-position attention — for example raising a detector's sensitivity during an entity's likely hours, or weighting correlation priors.
- Off by default, with the behaviour change visible in logs when enabled.
- `query_pattern`'s hourly and daily marginals surface as a small per-entity chart on the Entities page, so the learned memory is legible to a human.

### Definition of Done

- A consumer reads `query_likelihood` and changes an observable behavior with it (detector sensitivity or a correlation prior), behind a flag that is off by default.
- With the flag on, the log shows what the memory contributed to a decision; with it off, behavior is identical to today.
- A test drives a recorded pattern through the consumer and asserts the decision differs from the no-memory case.
### Current state: stubbed

The correlator writes to the state-space memory and increments its counters. Nothing reads it back: `query_likelihood` and `query_pattern` have no callers outside tests, so `state_space_memory_enabled` currently buys a growing table and no behaviour.

This shipped as scaffolding, not as a finished feature — it was not merged as done because it had not been thought through far enough. Anyone picking it up is welcome to do it better than the sketch suggests, including changing the seam if the seam is wrong. The bar for merging the finished version is the same as for anything else here.

issues.title: [SPIKE] One semantic graph for identity and state space?
issues.body:
### Context

Identity is already RDF-shaped without saying so: taxonomy references are CURIEs, the equivalence store is a `sameAs` graph with a hand-rolled transitive closure, the entity taxonomy is a subclass tree, and entity typing is type inference. There are now four parallel taxonomy systems, and every new classifier adds resolution logic to each.

### ASRs

- Decide whether identity and the cognitive state space should sit on one RDF/SKOS graph instead of four bespoke resolvers, and how far to take it: shared semantics only, an embedded triple store, or query support.
- Weigh it against the hardware floor — memory, dependencies, and the Python version the station runs.
- Deliverable is an ADR with a recommendation, not an implementation.

### Definition of Done

A written decision the next identity change can be built against.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Finish the weather integration — real gateway parsing and a dashboard card
issues.body:
### Context

Weather ingestion ships with the provider seam deliberately unfinished: `EcowittProvider._parse` raises rather than guess at a response format nobody has captured. Detections can already carry weather context, but no station is actually reading a gateway, and the dashboard has nowhere to show conditions.

### ASRs

- Capture a real response from a deployed gateway and map its fields to the reading model, converting imperial units to SI. Do not invent the field names — read them off the device.
- Show current conditions on the dashboard alongside detection activity.
- Absent or stale weather stays invisible rather than rendering an empty card.

### Definition of Done

- `EcowittProvider._parse` maps fields captured from a real gateway response, converting imperial units to SI, with the captured sample kept as a test fixture.
- The ingestor survives a full poll cycle against that gateway without raising, and a detection recorded during it carries weather context.
- The dashboard shows current conditions for a station that has a gateway configured, and shows nothing for one that does not.
### Current state: stubbed

`EcowittProvider._parse` raises `NotImplementedError` on every call and the ingest loop re-raises rather than absorbing it, so `orpheus-weather` exits on its first poll. Nothing reaches the dashboard card, and no station is reading a gateway today.

This shipped as scaffolding, not as a finished feature — it was not merged as done because it had not been thought through far enough. Anyone picking it up is welcome to do it better than the sketch suggests, including changing the seam if the seam is wrong. The bar for merging the finished version is the same as for anything else here.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Let the config store back OrpheusConfig
issues.body:
### Context

The layered, versioned config store exists and nothing reads it: agents still load YAML plus environment directly. The remaining step is delegation, and it has a trap. The store returns environment values as raw strings, while the existing config coerces them to the declared type. Delegating without reconciling that would silently change types across every agent.

### ASRs

- Reconcile type coercion first — give the store a typed read that honours the same defaults-derived types.
- Delegate the main config lookup to the store while keeping YAML as the base layer and environment as the highest priority.
- Agents re-read tunables when the store announces a change, instead of requiring a restart.
- Off by default until an operator opts in; with it off, behaviour is unchanged.

### Definition of Done

- The store exposes a typed read that honors the same defaults-derived coercion `OrpheusConfig` applies today, with tests covering the types that differ from raw strings.
- `OrpheusConfig` delegates to the store, and every component's existing config tests pass unchanged.
- An operator can change a tunable value at runtime and a component picks it up without a restart or a YAML edit.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Per-species confidence thresholds for bird detection
issues.body:
### Context

One global confidence threshold decides every species. That is wrong in both directions: common, loud, well-modelled species clear it on noise, while quiet or under-represented ones never clear it at all. The threshold is a single number standing in for hundreds of different detection problems.

### ASRs

- Per-species thresholds, defaulting to the global value when a species has no entry.
- Calibration derived from recorded detections rather than hand-tuned guesses, with the method written down.
- Operators can override any species locally.

### Definition of Done

- A per-species threshold table is read at detection time, falling back to the global value where a species has no entry.
- The calibration method is written down and derived from recorded detections, not hand-picked.
- Re-running a recorded set through the new thresholds is reported as a before/after count per species, so the change is measured rather than asserted.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Species suppression list for public sharing
issues.body:
### Context

Publishing detections publicly can expose the location of a sensitive species — nesting raptors, anything poached or disturbed by visitors. Conservation data-sharing conventions handle this with suppression lists; Orpheus has no such control, so anything shared publicly is shared completely.

### ASRs

- An operator-maintained list of species that are withheld or coarsened in any public-facing output.
- Suppression applies to exports and to the read-only portal, not to the local database — the station keeps its own record.
- Ships with sensible defaults documented, and a clear statement that the operator is responsible for their jurisdiction's rules.

### Definition of Done

- An operator-maintained suppression list withholds or coarsens the listed species in exports and in the read-only portal, while the local database keeps the full record.
- A suppressed species cannot be recovered from a public artifact — not from a coordinate, a clip, or a count.
- Tests cover both output paths, and the list's location and format are documented for the operator.

issues.title: [REFACTOR] One clip-existence check, shared
issues.body:
### Context

Whether an audio clip still exists on disk is decided in more than one place, with slightly different path handling. The database outlives the files it points at, so this check runs on hot UI paths and needs to answer the same way everywhere.

### ASRs

- A single helper in the shared library resolves a clip path and reports existence.
- The UI and any other caller use it rather than re-deriving paths.
- Behaviour for missing clips is unchanged — the UI still degrades gracefully.

### Definition of Done

- One helper in the shared library resolves a clip path and reports existence; the UI and every other caller use it.
- No second path-resolution or existence check remains in the tree.
- The UI's behavior for a missing clip is unchanged, pinned by its existing tests.

issues.title: [INFRA] Re-link detection chains recorded before chain ownership was fixed
issues.body:
### Context

Detections record which audio-motion event they came from, which is how the dashboard groups a sighting. Rows written before that ownership was corrected have no such link, so old history renders as disconnected fragments while recent history groups correctly.

### ASRs

- A one-time, idempotent, resumable migration that re-links historical children to their originating event using clip path and timestamp proximity.
- Runs with a dry-run mode that reports what it would change before anything is written.
- Refuses to guess when evidence is ambiguous, and reports how many rows it left alone.

### Definition of Done

Old history groups the same way new history does, or is honestly reported as unlinkable.

issues.title: [MLOPS] Automated Acoustic Regression Testing (Golden Dataset)
issues.body:
### Context

When we update BirdNET or AVES models, how do we know accuracy hasn't regressed? Build a CI pipeline step that tests new models against a "Golden Dataset" — a curated set of audio recordings with known-correct species labels. If accuracy drops below a threshold, the pipeline blocks the merge.

No regressions in production. Ever.

### Architecturally Significant Requirements (ASRs)

**Interface (Contract):**
- CLI: `orpheus-model-eval --model <path> --dataset <path> --threshold <float> --output <report_path>`.
- `ModelEvaluator` class with methods: `evaluate(model_path: str, dataset_path: str) -> EvaluationReport`.
- `EvaluationReport` dataclass: `{"overall_accuracy": float, "per_species": Dict[str, SpeciesMetrics], "passed": bool, "threshold": float}`.
- `SpeciesMetrics` dataclass: `{"precision": float, "recall": float, "f1": float, "sample_count": int}`.
- CI output: Markdown report posted as PR comment.

**Implementation (Internal Logic):**
- Golden Dataset stored in Git LFS or DVC with manifest file listing audio paths and ground-truth labels.
- Inference runner: load model, process each audio file, collect predictions.
- Metric calculator: per-species precision/recall/F1 plus overall accuracy.
- Regression gate: fail if any species F1 drops more than threshold (default 5%) vs. baseline.

### Architectural Constraints

- Golden Dataset must be stored in a reproducible location (Git LFS, S3, or DVC — not checked into the repo directly).
- Evaluation metrics: precision, recall, F1 per species, plus overall accuracy.
- Threshold for blocking must be configurable (default: no species drops more than 5% F1).
- Pipeline must produce a human-readable report (Markdown or HTML) attached to the PR.
- Must be Python 3.9 compatible.

### Acceptance Criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Automated Acoustic Regression Testing

  Scenario: Model passes regression check
    Given a Golden Dataset with 50 labeled recordings
    And the baseline model achieves 0.85 F1 for American Crow
    When the new model achieves 0.87 F1 for American Crow
    Then the regression check passes
    And the PR report shows improvement for American Crow

  Scenario: Model fails regression check
    Given a Golden Dataset with 50 labeled recordings
    And the baseline model achieves 0.85 F1 for American Crow
    When the new model achieves 0.78 F1 for American Crow (> 5% drop)
    Then the regression check fails
    And the CI pipeline blocks the merge
    And the PR report highlights the regression

  Scenario: Generate human-readable report
    Given a completed model evaluation
    When the report is generated
    Then it contains per-species precision, recall, and F1 scores
    And it clearly marks regressions vs. improvements
```

### Definition of Done

- [ ] Golden Dataset curated with at least 50 labeled recordings covering the top 10 detected species.
- [ ] Evaluation script that runs inference and computes per-species metrics.
- [ ] CI pipeline step that runs on model-update PRs and blocks on regression.
- [ ] Report template showing before/after metrics in the PR comment.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Collapse hierarchical audio labels in the Audio Events view
issues.body:
### Context

The general-purpose audio classifier emits hierarchical labels, so one cricket can light up several rows at once — the specific label and every ancestor. The view shows all of them, which reads as several events rather than one.

### ASRs

- An option to collapse a parent label when a more specific child fired in the same window.
- Off by default so the raw classifier output stays visible for anyone comparing against it.
- The counts stay honest — collapsing changes presentation, not the underlying data.

### Definition of Done

- An off-by-default option collapses a parent label when a more specific child fired in the same window.
- With it off, the view shows exactly what it shows today.
- Collapsing changes presentation only: the underlying counts and stored rows are untouched, and a test asserts the totals match before and after.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Home Assistant integration
issues.body:
### Context

Orpheus already knows what it heard and when. A home automation hub is where most people already ask questions out loud, so the natural interface for "what birds did Orpheus hear in the last five minutes?" is a voice assistant backed by Home Assistant rather than a dashboard someone has to open.

### ASRs

- Publish entity events to Home Assistant in a form it understands natively — MQTT discovery is the low-friction path (HA auto-creates sensors from retained discovery topics) and the mosquitto fallback backend already exists; a REST/webhook push is the alternative if the bridge should not depend on the legacy transport.
- Expose at minimum: last detection (species, confidence, time, channel), a rolling count per window, and a per-species "last seen" so HA automations and voice queries can read them.
- Off by default and additive: a disabled integration must leave the event bus and the database byte-identical to today.
- Document the HA-side setup (what appears, what to name it, an example automation and a voice query) for someone who runs HA but has never seen Orpheus internals.

### Definition of Done

With the integration enabled, a stock Home Assistant install discovers Orpheus sensors without manual YAML, a voice query for recent detections answers correctly, and turning the flag off returns the system to its current behavior.

issues.title: [INFRA] Make the end-to-end test harness install opt-in
issues.body:
### Context

A plain `make install` pulls the Playwright end-to-end harness and downloads a Chromium browser, which surprises anyone installing Orpheus to run it rather than to develop it. The download is documented now, but documenting a surprise is weaker than removing it.

### ASRs

- The UI component's `install` target sets up what running the dashboard needs; the browser-driving harness moves behind a separate target (for example `install-e2e`).
- CI keeps running the e2e suite — the workflow calls the new target explicitly.
- `make test-e2e` fails with a clear message telling the developer which target to run when the harness is absent.

### Definition of Done

A fresh `make install` completes without downloading a browser, CI still runs the e2e suite, and the quickstarts no longer need to warn about an unexpected download.

issues.title: [BUG] Intermittent abort during the event-bus test teardown
issues.body:
### Context

One run of the full test suite died with `Abort trap: 6` — a process-level crash, not a test failure — while the JetStream tests were skipping for want of a broker. The suite has not reproduced it in eleven subsequent runs (with a broker, without one, and targeted at the event-bus tests), and the failing run happened while several processes were rewriting files in the same tree, which can abort an interpreter mid-import. A rare race in the bus's thread-and-loop teardown cannot be ruled out on that evidence alone.

### ASRs

- Reproduce or exclude: run the event-bus suites in a loop under stress (no broker, broker appearing and disappearing mid-run) and capture the crash log if it recurs.
- If it is the teardown path, the fix belongs where the connect-abort flag and the teardown budget live; add a regression test that pins the sequence.
- If it is environmental, record that finding so the next person who sees it does not re-investigate.

### Definition of Done

Either a reproduction with a fix and a test, or a written verdict that the crash was environmental, with the evidence that supports it.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Enforce the file-retention age window
issues.body:
### Context

`storage.retention.raw_audio_days` and `raw_video_days` are read and validated at startup and then ignored. Clip cleanup runs on size alone: a directory is swept when it passes `cleanup_trigger_percent` of `max_size_gb`, oldest first. A station under its size budget therefore keeps clips indefinitely while the config claims a 30-day window — the same "setting that pretends to exist" problem as *Enforce detections_days — retention for database rows*, one layer up.

### The migration hazard, which is the hard part

Turning this on is not a normal feature flip. Because the windows have never been applied, running stations are holding far more history than their configured window implies: a box that has kept a year of clips under a `30` setting loses eleven months of them on the first pass. Deleted clips are not in the standard pre-upgrade backup. Any implementation that deletes on first run without warning is wrong, however correct its cleanup logic is.

### ASRs

- A dry-run/report mode that lists what a pass *would* remove — file count and total bytes, per directory — without deleting anything, runnable before an operator commits to enforcement.
- First enforcement is opt-in rather than a side effect of upgrading: an operator who upgrades and changes nothing must not lose clips.
- The pass logs its effective policy and what it removed, in the same shape as the size-triggered cleanup.
- `min_file_age_hours` still floors deletion, and the size trigger still runs on what age retention leaves behind.
- The upgrade path is documented: how to see what would go, and how to widen the window first if the answer is more than intended.

### Definition of Done

An operator can see exactly what enabling the window would delete before enabling it, upgrading without touching the config never deletes a clip, and disk headroom accounts for both age and size.

### Current state: stubbed

The keys are parsed and validated at startup and read by nothing. An implementation was prototyped and reverted — it enforced age on every pass with no dry run, which would have deleted history on upgrade — along with a `min_free_space_percent` backstop that triggered cleanup on filesystem free space regardless of the configured budget. That backstop is worth reconsidering as part of this work; it was reverted with the rest, not rejected on its merits.

This shipped as scaffolding, not as a finished feature — it was not merged as done because it had not been thought through far enough. Anyone picking it up is welcome to do it better than the sketch suggests, including changing the seam if the seam is wrong. The bar for merging the finished version is the same as for anything else here.

Related: *[HARDWARE] Retention steady-state review: size-trigger economics on the data disk* decides what the windows and caps should be; this story is the mechanism that makes a window mean anything.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Show which database the dashboard is reading
issues.body:
### Context

`ui.read_from_replica` points the dashboard at a mirror snapshot instead of the live database. When the replica is asked for but cannot be served — `mirror.staging_path` unset on the reading host, the snapshot not produced yet, the mirror disabled or broken — the routing falls back to the live database and records a warning in the journal. On a portal host there is no live database, so the fallback opens an empty one and every page renders blank with nothing on screen to explain why.

An operator looking at a blank dashboard cannot tell live from replica, or a working replica from a silent fallback, without reading logs on a different machine.

### ASRs

- The routing decision — which database was opened, and whether it was the one requested — is recorded where the UI can serve it.
- Diagnostics shows the current source, and says plainly when the replica was requested and is not being served.
- No behavior change to the fallback itself: this makes an existing decision visible, it does not alter what the UI reads.

### Definition of Done

An operator can tell from the dashboard alone whether they are looking at live data or a replica, and a silent fallback becomes a visible one.

### Current state

A prototype was built and reverted from the release-polish branch as feature work rather than polish. The routing that needs to expose its decision lives in the UI backend's `db.py`; the reverted sketch recorded the decision there, served it from a diagnostics endpoint, and banked it in the Diagnostics page. Anyone picking it up is welcome to do it better than the sketch suggests, including changing the seam if the seam is wrong.
